answer_text:
Let  

\[
B_L=\left\{(x,y):\sqrt{(x-7)^2+(y+3)^2}<L\right\}
\]

be the open ball centered at \(t=(7,-3)\). We want the largest \(L\) such that \(G\) is invertible on \(B_L\).

The map is

\[
G(x,y)=\bigl((x-1)^2,\;y^4\bigr).
\]

Non-injectivity can occur because:

\[
(x-1)^2=(u-1)^2 \iff u=x \text{ or } u=2-x,
\]

and

\[
y^4=v^4 \iff v=y \text{ or } v=-y.
\]

So two distinct points in the ball can map to the same value if the ball crosses the symmetry lines \(x=1\) or \(y=0\).

From the center \(t=(7,-3)\):

- distance to the line \(x=1\) is \(|7-1|=6\);
- distance to the line \(y=0\) is \(|-3|=3\).

The closer symmetry line is \(y=0\), so the largest possible radius should be \(L=3\).

Now check that \(L=3\) works. If \((x,y)\in B_3\), then

\[
\sqrt{(x-7)^2+(y+3)^2}<3
\]

implies

\[
4<x<10,\qquad -6<y<0.
\]

Thus \(x-1>0\) and \(y<0\). On this region,

\[
x\mapsto (x-1)^2
\]

is one-to-one, and

\[
y\mapsto y^4
\]

is one-to-one because \(y<0\). Therefore \(G\) is one-to-one on \(B_3\). Its Jacobian determinant is

\[
\det DG(x,y)=
\begin{vmatrix}
2(x-1)&0\\
0&4y^3
\end{vmatrix}
=8(x-1)y^3,
\]

which is nonzero on \(B_3\), so the inverse is smooth there.

Now suppose \(L>3\). Choose \(a>0\) such that

\[
0<a<\min(3,L-3).
\]

Then the two distinct points

\[
p=(7,-a),\qquad q=(7,a)
\]

both lie in \(B_L\), since

\[
\|p-t\|=3-a<L,\qquad \|q-t\|=3+a<L.
\]

But

\[
G(p)=G(q)=\bigl(6^2,a^4\bigr)=(36,a^4),
\]

so \(G\) is not one-to-one on \(B_L\). Hence no \(L>3\) works.

Therefore the largest possible value is

\[
\boxed{3}
\]
